title: Candidate to Codebase Handshake — 72hr Onboard
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact cross-functional playbook that closes the loop between candidate/hire evaluation and the first technical impact: shipping a small, reviewable PR within the first 72 hours. Designed for IC engineering hires (mid-level to senior), the doc bundles a short hiring rubric, quick-hire signals, and a day-by-day onboarding checklist that the hiring manager, buddy, and people ops can follow.

Scope and assumptions:
- New hire has accepted offer and has day-zero access requests submitted by HR.
- Role is a product/backend/frontend engineer expected to make code contributions within first week.
- This is intentionally lightweight — meant to maximize early momentum and reduce cognitive overhead.

Hiring signals that map to 72hr success (used at offer stage):
- Ship-first mentality: candidate demonstrates examples of small, end-to-end changes shipped in past 3 months.
- Fast-feedback loop experience: uses code reviews and CI effectively in prior roles.
- Local dev competency: can explain how they run a local build/test cycle.
- Communication: clear in async updates and able to write concise PR descriptions.

Interview rubric (condensed, 1–4 scale per row, used by hiring panel to align expectations):
- System oriented (design small feature): 1–4 — looks for trade-aware decisions, not full architecture.
- Code fluency (practices & patterns): 1–4 — idiomatic patterns, simple refactor suggestions.
- Debugging & tests: 1–4 — writes or explains unit/integ tests, can triage a failing test.
- Collaboration: 1–4 — communicates clearly, handles ambiguity, raises prioritization questions.
- First-week plan readiness: 1–4 — candidate can list reasonable first-three tasks post-hire.

Score interpretation (panel guidance):
- 16–20: strong fit for rapid shipping; prioritize schedule for early PR.
- 11–15: OK fit; ensure extra onboarding bandwidth from buddy.
- <=10: re-evaluate scope of early-impact targets.

Day-zero (pre-boarding checklist, people ops + IT) — complete before new hire’s start time:
- Accounts provisioned: Google identity, GitHub org invite, Jira/Linear account, Okta SSO linked.
- Repo access: read + branch privileges for the base service-template repo.
- Machine request: if company laptop, imaged with standard dev snapshot; otherwise, onboarding notes for personal machine config.
- Slack invite and channel additions (team #, onboarding #, #dev-help).
- Key admin links sent: PKI/KMS request doc, security policies, VPN/VPC access request form.

Day 1 (orientation + environment build — target: green local build):
- Morning: 30m welcome from manager (context, immediate expectations — 72hr PR).
- Manager delivers 1-paragraph goal: "By EOD day 3: small feature or fix with tests, merged to main via normal review path."
- Buddy assignment: buddy name, 1:1 scheduled daily for first 5 days (15–20m).
- Workspace setup checklist for hire (step-by-step links):
  - Clone service-template repo, install toolchain, run scripts/install.sh.
  - Run full test suite subset: smoke tests locally; ensure all linters run.
  - Start local dev server, hit example endpoint.
- Quick read list (30–60 minutes):
  - README of primary repo, CONTRIBUTING.md, architecture-one-pager, recent INC/PR linked to the service.
- Small starter task assigned (issue created pre-day1): pick a low-risk bug or doc fix that exercises the full loop.

Day 2 (context + first change — target: draft PR):
- Morning sync (10m) with manager: confirm PR target and clarify acceptance criteria.
- Buddy co-work: pair for 60–90m on the branch creation + tests. Buddy helps with test harness and CI quirks.
- Draft PR created by end of day with description template: problem, changes, how to test locally, testing done, roll-out notes.
- Add reviewers: at least one teammate from immediate squad + one cross-team reviewer depending on the area.

Day 3 (review loop + merge — target: merged PR):
- Address review comments quickly — keep PR small to reduce iteration time.
- If CI failures, escalate to buddy or SRE contact listed in the onboarding page.
- Merge when green and follow standard release flow (feature flags if required).
- Post-merge: short async announcement to team channel with what shipped and why.

Mentor rotation & responsibilities (first week):
- Buddy (primary): day-to-day blocker removal, code review primer, test infra help.
- Manager: sets goals, prioritizes deliverables, provides context on product impact.
- Pair reviewers: rotate the reviewer for early PRs so the hire sees multiple styles and standards.

Interview-to-onboard handoff template (to be filled by hiring manager on offer acceptance and attached to HR ticket):
- Candidate strengths (3 bullets).
- Potential friction areas (3 bullets).
- Suggested first-PR task (link to a pre-created issue).
- Assigned buddy.

Security & compliance quick checks (non-exhaustive):
- Confirm signed policies and required training modules completed (security basics, data handling).
- Repo-specific secrets access gated behind KMS request — do not store keys locally.
- If private deploys team is involved, ensure VPC access requests are queued.

Success criteria and signals after 7 days and 30 days:
- 72hr goal: green local build, one merged PR, at least one review given by the new hire.
- 7-day: participates in standups, closes 1–2 follow-up tickets, demonstrates CI knowledge.
- 30-day: owns a small feature or improvement, writes at least one design note, feedback loop from peer reviews is positive.

Escalation and troubleshooting quick contacts (use Slack first, then email for infra ops):
- Buddy Slack: @buddy-name
- Eng SRE on-call: #sre-oncall (pin list in repo README)
- People Ops escalation: people-ops@redwood.com

Open questions & improvements (for post-mortem after pilot runs):
- Should we require the hiring panel to nominate the starter issue at offer stage?
- Is 72 hours realistic for non-US time zones with provisioning delays? Consider gating by region.
- How to scale the buddy program without overloading senior ICs?

Appendix: PR description template (to paste in PR body):
- Title: concise summary (area: short description)
- Background: why this change matters (1–2 sentences)
- Changes: bullet list of code/behavior changes
- How to test locally: exact commands and env vars
- Testing done: unit/integration/manual steps performed
- Rollout notes: feature flags, migration steps (if any)

Notes to people-ops/manager: this doc is intentionally compact. For full onboarding flow include links to the master onboards index. Track time-to-first-merge metric for hires as a leading indicator of onboarding friction; report monthly to people-ops.

Document history:
- 2025-05-12: initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2025-05-15: added rubric thresholds and linked artifacts (Jonah Kim)
